Threshold or deblur an image to binarize features

Source: R/LilHelpers3.R
image_threshold.Rd

Turns a grayscale image into a binary one, either against a single image-wide level (method = "global") or against the local brightness around each pixel (method = "adaptive"). A separate deblur = TRUE mode instead separates two layers of a segmented image.

Usage

image_threshold(
  img,
  threshold = 0.4,
  method = "global",
  adaptive_k = 1.15,
  window_size = 51,
  select_layer = 2,
  mask_layer = 1,
  binary_01 = FALSE,
  deblur = FALSE,
  invert = FALSE
)

Arguments

img

SpatRaster object.

threshold

Fraction of the global maximum, between 0 and 1, used by method = "global" and by deblur = TRUE. Not used by method = "adaptive", which takes adaptive_k instead.

method

"global" or "adaptive". Ignored when deblur = TRUE.

adaptive_k

Multiple of the local mean a pixel must reach to count as foreground, for method = "adaptive" only. Must be above 1 for the method to separate anything; see the section above.

window_size

Odd integer, the side of the local-mean box in pixels, for method = "adaptive" only.

select_layer

Integer or NULL. Which layer to threshold or deblur. If NULL and the image is multilayer, the mean of all layers is used.

mask_layer

Integer or NULL. If set, this layer is thresholded against its own level rather than against select_layer's.

binary_01

Logical. If TRUE, the output is 0/1; if FALSE, it keeps the maximum value of the input.

deblur

Logical. If TRUE, runs the deblurring mode instead of thresholding.

invert

Logical. FALSE, the default, keeps the pixels at or above the cut, so the brighter side is the foreground: roots on a dark tray. TRUE keeps the pixels at or below it, for the commoner flatbed case of dark roots on a bright tray. threshold remains a fraction of the image maximum and adaptive_k a factor on the local mean; with invert = TRUE the local cut is the mean divided by adaptive_k rather than multiplied by it. Ignored when deblur = TRUE.

Value

SpatRaster object.

Global thresholding

A pixel is foreground when it is at least threshold times the brightest value in the image. One level for the whole image, so it only works when the illumination is even: a flatbed scan with a bright center and dark corners has no single level that is right everywhere.

Adaptive thresholding

A pixel is foreground when it is at least adaptive_k times the mean of the window_size x window_size box around it. The reference level follows the illumination, so a brightness gradient leaves the decision unchanged.

Two constraints decide whether it works, and both are properties of the image rather than preferences:

adaptive_k must exceed 1. In a window holding only background the local mean is the background level, so about half the background sits above it. At adaptive_k = 1 roughly half of a root-free patch therefore comes out as root, and below 1 nearly all of it does. The method needs a dead band above 1, and the band has to clear the background's own noise: the noisier the background, the larger adaptive_k has to be. Its upper bound is the root-to-background brightness ratio – past that the roots fail their own test and nothing is found. The default suits a reasonably clean scan; a noisy one wants more, and a scan with little root-to-background contrast leaves no useful range at all.

window_size must be large compared with the widest root. The window average includes the root itself, so a root that fills much of its own window raises its own reference level and is rejected. Recall is what fails first: the roots are suppressed rather than the background. A window several times the widest root is a reasonable starting point; measure the widest root in pixels on one scan and scale from there, since a root's pixel width depends on the scan resolution. A larger window also leaves the full root-to-background contrast available, so it allows a larger adaptive_k; set the window first, then the multiplier. Going large costs little, because the local mean is computed as two 1-D passes and so scales with the window side rather than its square.

What neither method can do

Both methods mark pixels that are brighter than a reference, so they separate bright features on a darker background and nothing else. Where root and soil are about equally bright, the useful range for adaptive_k closes: the margin the background noise demands is larger than the root-to-background contrast allows, and no setting works. The bundled minirhizotron scan is such an image – scored against the segmentation shipped with it, its roots are not reliably brighter than the surrounding soil, and the soil's own texture varies more than root differs from soil. That is a property of the image rather than of the implementation, and tuning does not rescue it. Scans like it need a trained segmenter such as RootDetector, whose binary output the rest of Rootopia reads directly.

Deblurring

deblur = TRUE ignores method. It subtracts select_layer from mask_layer and thresholds both at threshold times the maximum of select_layer, which separates in-focus structure from an out-of-focus halo in a two-layer segmented image.

Examples

img = terra::rast(seg_Oulanka2023_Session03_T067)
image_threshold(img, threshold = 0.3, method = "global")
#> class       : SpatRaster
#> size        : 1161, 4900, 3  (nrow, ncol, nlyr)
#> resolution  : 1, 1  (x, y)
#> extent      : 0, 4900, 0, 1161  (xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax)
#> coord. ref. : 
#> source(s)   : memory
#> names       : lyr.1, lyr.2, lyr.2
#> min values  :     0,     0,     0
#> max values  :   255,   255,   255
image_threshold(img, threshold = 0.4, select_layer = 2, mask_layer = 1, deblur = TRUE)
#> class       : SpatRaster
#> size        : 1161, 4900, 3  (nrow, ncol, nlyr)
#> resolution  : 1, 1  (x, y)
#> extent      : 0, 4900, 0, 1161  (xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax)
#> coord. ref. : 
#> source(s)   : memory
#> names       : lyr.1, lyr.2, lyr.2
#> min values  :     0,     0,     0
#> max values  :   255,   255,   255

# Adaptive thresholding, on a small image that meets both conditions above:
# the background falls from 0.40 to 0.11 across the frame, a 3.6-fold range
# no single global level can follow, and three 1 px roots sit at twice their
# own local background. The window is far wider than the roots, and the
# multiplier is above 1.
m <- outer(seq(1, 0.4, length.out = 120), seq(1, 0.7, length.out = 120)) * 0.4
m[, c(20, 50, 90)] <- m[, c(20, 50, 90)] * 2
bw <- image_threshold(terra::rast(m), method = "adaptive",
                      adaptive_k = 1.15, window_size = 31, binary_01 = TRUE)
terra::plot(bw)
